circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, the Yas Marina Circuit spans 5. 281 kilometres and was designed by Hermann Tilke to host the Formula One season finale. The venue has served as the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix's home since 2009, making it the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit after Bahrain.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting motorsport events. Holding an FIA Grade 1 licence, the venue serves as a premier racing destination for multiple championship categories.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the 4. 326 km circuit was originally built as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following renovation and renaming to the A1-Ring, it returned as the Austrian Grand Prix host from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital that stretches 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The venue first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming a permanent fixture on the calendar with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix beginning in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 kilometers and hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. The FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates various motorsporting events including GP2 races, 24-hour endurance competitions, and features multiple track configurations for different series.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, is a 4. 657 km track featuring a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple aspects of car performance. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has hosted Formula One racing since 1950 and currently stages the Belgian Grand Prix. The venue has maintained continuous F1 competition since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km track that serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its primary role in international single-seater racing, the circuit has accommodated various other motorsport categories including sports car championships and North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading has hosted the Chinese Grand Prix intermittently, running annually from 2004 to 2019 before returning to the calendar in 2024. In addition to its Formula One commitments, the facility began hosting the Shanghai ePrix from 2024 onwards.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located in England near Northamptonshire, Silverstone Circuit has been the primary venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After decades of alternating with other British tracks, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km track near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc in 1986, marking a historic expansion of the sport into communist territories. Built remarkably quickly in just eight months near a major highway after the government rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park, the venue has since become a permanent fixture on the championship calendar.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located north of Milan, Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian circuit established in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track has hosted the Italian Grand Prix almost continuously since 1949, making it one of the longest-serving Formula One venues, and earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" through its characteristic high-speed straights and fast corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport facility situated in Mie Prefecture and managed by Honda Mobilityland. The venue, which accommodates 155,000 spectators, has become renowned as a premier destination for Formula One racing and the Japanese Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course situated in Paradise, Nevada, that navigates through the famous Las Vegas Boulevard district. The track weaves past iconic venues and entertainment establishments, featuring several of the city's most recognizable structures including major hotels and casino properties.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named after two fatal racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue returned to hosting Formula One in 2015 after a 23-year absence, having previously staged the Mexican Grand Prix on an earlier configuration until 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by specialist firm Apex Circuit Design, it was constructed specifically to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, encircling the harbour in the Principality of Monaco. It is widely known as Monte Carlo, particularly because the majority of the layout traverses the Monte Carlo neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the coastal dunes north of Zandvoort in the Netherlands, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the resurrected Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 to 2026. The track's nickname among enthusiasts, "The Roller coaster in the Dunes," stems from its undulating terrain with steeply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz that create dramatic elevation changes through the North Sea dunes.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari motor racing venue positioned north of Doha near the city of Lusail. Spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a principal straightaway measuring 1.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track hosts significant motorsport events and features an associated kart facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has served as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021. The circuit also began hosting an international electric racing series event starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang districts, utilizing public roads surrounding the Marina Bay waterfront as its racing surface.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of straightaways and varied cornering sections that test multiple driving skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that regularly hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major international motorsport events including MotoGP and endurance racing. Beyond its primary tenants, the track has also accommodated various touring car, rallycross, and sports car championships throughout its operational history.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand on the international circuit.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, bringing two championship titles from his 2005-2006 Renault campaigns and 32 career Grand Prix victories across 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved rare endurance racing success, including 24 Hours of Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One's and endurance racing's top championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured the 2026 Formula One drivers' title with Mercedes, setting a record as the sport's youngest champion, having claimed nine race victories since entering the championship in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, where he represents the team in the championship.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team. He brings his competitive spirit to one of the sport's most ambitious new projects in the grid.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish competitor, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One following a distinguished career that included two runner-up championship finishes with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. Over 13 seasons, the driver has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto, an Argentine racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for the Alpine team. He represents his nation in the sport's top racing category.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian motorsport competitor, holds a reserve driver position with Haas in Formula One while participating in seven championship races between 2024 and 2025. Beyond his F1 involvement, he actively races in endurance competitions, having driven for Nielsen Racing in the European Le Mans Series and currently competing in the LMP2 category for AF Corse in the Asian Le Mans Series.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly represents France in Formula One, currently driving for Alpine. The French driver achieved a notable victory at Monza in 2020 while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver currently competing for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, racing under the French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British driver Lewis Hamilton competes for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured seven world championship titles that match Michael Schumacher's record. Hamilton also holds multiple all-time records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One and has achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, including a Le Mans 24 Hours victory with Porsche in 2015.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver racing for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine-season career in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who has competed across multiple racing series, including two separate stints in Formula One between 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he races for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship and competes part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver racing for McLaren who secured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has claimed 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon recently drove for Haas in Formula One, having previously achieved his sole F1 victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while racing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac after spending 15 seasons in the sport, during which he has claimed six race victories. He finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while racing for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, has secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the series four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," he has since retired from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant contested two seasons of Formula One racing between 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously raced in the LMP2 class for Era Motorsport in the IMSA series.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One, where he drives for the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently serving as a reserve for both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After competing full-time in the sport from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a reserve role starting in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch racing driver Max Verstappen has captured four consecutive Formula One world titles with Red Bull Racing between 2021 and 2024, establishing himself as one of the sport's most dominant competitors. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories while continuing his tenure with the Milton Keynes-based team.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a racing driver currently functioning in a reserve capacity for Cadillac in Formula One. The driver competed actively in the series from 2022 through 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese competitor to have participated in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team operated as Renault's official Formula One entry from 2021 onwards, adopting the Alpine brand name to align with Renault's sports car division. Following Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025, the team transitioned away from its long-standing manufacturer-backed status.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One across multiple eras under different organizational structures, with the contemporary iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team name.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished competitor, participating in every championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" for their distinctive emblem, Ferrari remains the winningest team in the sport's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American Formula One team in 2014, which debuted in the 2016 championship season. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering firm established in 1970, the Sauber team initially excelled in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. After 32 seasons as one of motorsport's most enduring entries, the organization was purchased by Audi in 2024 and ceased operations at the end of 2025.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its dedicated Technology Centre in Woking, Surrey. Operating as a subsidiary within the broader McLaren Group, the team is wholly owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has been a fixture in Formula One since 1954 in both manufacturing and team ownership capacities. The current iteration, Mercedes-AMG Petronas, operates from Brackley under a German licence and became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and Toto Wolff from 2022 onward. The team carries the storied "Silver Arrows" nickname associated with Mercedes racing heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as Red Bull's second team. Based in Faenza with a presence in Milton Keynes, it operates alongside Red Bull Racing under the same Austrian ownership structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned squads. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates as Red Bull's second constructor alongside Red Bull Racing.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from its English base, emerged in 2005 as part of Red Bull GmbH's involvement in Formula One, where it remains one of two teams controlled by the energy drink conglomerate. Christian Horner led the squad from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies assuming leadership responsibilities in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and remains one of motorsport's historically significant operations.
